subject: Temporary burst replication: approval checklist & DPA/subprocessor notes
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbuspay.com>, DPO Team <dpo@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Temporary burst replication: initial ask and checklist

Hi Samira / Nimbus DPO team —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As discussed, NimbusPay wants a short "burst" replication window (up to 48 hours) into our APAC region for a time-bound analytics job tied to a vendor audit. The ask is explicitly temporary; production traffic and customer-serving inference must remain EU-pinned.

To move this forward I’ve attached a procurement checklist and a DPA excerpt that highlights our standard transient-processing carveout. Can you confirm the following on your side so we can route approvals?

- Acceptance of transient replication for analytics only (no customer-facing inference)
- Desired start/end window (we propose 2027-06-22 to 2027-06-24)
- Any required contractual amendment or a signed addendum to the DPA (we can provision a one-page rider)
- Whether you need KMS key scoping or separate key encryption for the sampled dataset

Internal asks: Marissa — can you attach the current subprocessor roster and mark any APAC compute partners that would be touched? Karthik — can you confirm replication encryption in transit and whether we can keep KV cache TTLs local to EU during the window (prefer no KV shipping for inference cache). Laura — procurement signoff checklist please.

I’ve copied the proposed timeline and a DocuSign link for the addendum if Nimbus is comfortable.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: procurement-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-dpa-excerpt-2027.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbuspay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Temporary burst replication: initial ask and checklist

Alex — thanks for laying this out. Couple quick clarifying questions from our DPO: 

1) Will any logs or telemetry generated during the burst be egressed to non-EU locations (we need to confirm for our auditors)?
2) Can Redwood provide a short, timeboxed attestation that no model weights or model updates will be made available in APAC during the window?
3) For the KMS ask: we prefer to scope a customer-controlled key if possible, but if not, we need confirmation the keys used are geo-restricted and access is logged.

Also, we’ll need the full subprocessor roster (not just APAC partners) for our procurement and security review — can you include contact points for escalation?

Samira
Samira Khan
Director of Privacy & Compliance
NimbusPay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbuspay.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Temporary burst replication: subprocessor roster + DPA excerpt

Hi Samira — attaching the full subprocessor roster (CSV) and a highlighted DPA excerpt that calls out our temporary-replication process. Notes: 

- APAC compute will be our partner "CloudNode APAC" (listed in row 18). That partner is used only for transient analytics and does not serve production inference for NimbusPay.
- Logging: audit logs for replication jobs are kept and retained for 90 days by default; we can extend retention to 12 months for this engagement if required.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on dedicated plans; for hosted customers we offer customer-scoped keys with audit logging. For this short window we recommend scoped customer keys — procurement can make the call.

I’ve included a short escalation contact column in the roster. If Nimbus signs the one-page rider we can lock the dates and trigger ops runbook execution.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Legal Ops & Partner Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor-roster-2027.csv (CSV stub), redwood-dpa-excerpt-2027.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Temporary burst replication: technical caveats and runbook items

Samira / Alex / Marissa — technical clarifications from infra: 

- We will perform replication at object-store level; no model artifact movement. I can confirm model weights and runtime images are not promoted to APAC nodes for this job.
- KV cache: we will not ship inference KV caches. The analytics job will use a read-only snapshot of the dataset and streaming jobs will be isolated to a separate analytics cluster.
- Logs: replication logs and job telemetry will be written to an EU-central logging bucket. If Nimbus requests, we can provision a time-limited, read-only export of aggregated job metrics to an APAC bucket for the analytics team (this would be a separate approval).
- KMS: customer-managed key is supported on a per-customer scope. If Nimbus supplies a key, data-at-rest in the APAC temporary bucket will be encrypted with that key and access will be logged.

Ops caveat: we require at least 10 business days lead time to schedule the window on the APAC pool and to run the security checklist. If Nimbus needs earlier, we can do a short-notice window but it will require SLA exception approval.

Tech runbook (high-level) attached as part of the procurement checklist.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Temporary burst replication: procurement signoff

Alex / Team — procurement review complete. Action items for formal signoff: 

1) Nimbus to sign the one-page DPA rider (DocuSign link shared).
2) Nimbus to confirm whether they will provide a customer-managed KMS key by 2027-06-18.
3) Ops schedule confirmed for proposed window pending the KMS decision; ops team will hold the APAC slot contingent on signed rider.

Samira — if you confirm the key approach and sign the rider, we will issue the final runbook and a short attestation that models are not deployed to APAC for the job.

Laura Bennett
VP, Procurement & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

One-line reply from Samira later: "Signing rider now; will confirm KMS by Friday." quoted inline in the DocuSign workflow.
